caseno: Civil Petition For Leave To Appeal No. 198 of 1997
lawyer:
Mr. B. Hossain, Deputy Attorney General, instructed by Mr. Sharifuddin Chaklader, Advocate-on-Record, For the Petitioner
Mr. Md. Abdus Samad, Advocate, instructed by Mr. Nawab Ali, Advocate-on-Record, For Respondent No.1
Respondent Nos. 2-3: Not represented
parties:
Bangladesh ------ Petitioner
Vs.
National Construction and Consult Ltd. and others ----- Respondents
full_judgment: Bimalendu Bikash Roy Choudhury, J: There was a contract between the Public Works Department of the Government of Bangladesh and respondent No. 1 National Construction and Consult Ltd., hereinafter referred to as the Contractor, for construction of Thana Health Complex at Tarail within the district of Kishoregonj. After the completion of the work the contractor made a claim of Tk. 66,17,000/- as compensation. This gave rise to a dispute which was referred to the sole Arbitrator namely, the Superintending Engineer, Mymensingh Circle. The Arbitrator gave his award in favour of the Contractor, but failed to file it in court or notify the parties. On 2 March 1986 the Contractor filed an application (Arbitration Suit No. 35 of 1986) before the Subordinate Judge, First Court Mymensingh under section 14(2) of the Arbitration Act for a direction upon the Arbitrator to file the award together with depositions and documents in court. The Government filed a written objection thereto. The Arbitrator filed his award on 30 June 1986. The notice of filing of the award was thereafter served on the parties but none raised any objection to the award within the specified time. In the circumstances the Contractor filed another application (Arbitration Suit No. 136 of 1986) praying for passing a decree in terms of the award. After analogous hearing of the matters the learned Subordinate Judge found no reason to set aside the award or to remit the same to the Arbitrator for reconsideration. Accordingly he made the award a Rule of the Court and pronounced a decree in accordance therewith. The Government preferred F.A. No. 22 of 1988 therefrom to the High Court Division. It was contended therein that the learned Subordinate Judge failed to notice that the Ministry of Works was not responsible for any loss suffered by the Contractor for force majeure and as such the Arbitrator had misconducted himself in awarding compensation to the Contractor. A Division Bench of the High Court Division did not accept the contention and dismissed the appeal by judgment and decree dated 18 November 1996, observing "It is well-settled that in an appeal u/s 39 of the Arbitration Act, the decision of the arbitrator cannot be reviewed and the appellate court cannot construct an award for the arbitrator and all that the appellate court has to see whether the award can be challenged on the ground of excess of jurisdiction or incompetence or misconduct as understood in law. Therefore if we have to consider the submission of the learned D.A.G. then we are to review the award which we cannot do under the law, so we do not find any merit in this appeal."
